faqs.q: How much does a Romanian Mioritic Shepherd Dog cost to buy?
faqs.a: Reputable breeders typically charge $1,200–$4,000 for a Romanian Mioritic Shepherd Dog puppy. Prices vary by breeder reputation, health testing, and lineage. Rescue adoption fees are typically $100–$500 and include vaccinations, neutering, and microchipping.

faqs.q: What is the monthly cost of owning a Romanian Mioritic Shepherd Dog?
faqs.a: Budget $200–$400 per month for a Romanian Mioritic Shepherd Dog, covering food, preventive vet care, insurance, grooming and supplies. Large breeds cost more across every category — food portions, medication doses and professional services all scale with weight.

faqs.q: What are the biggest ongoing costs for a Romanian Mioritic Shepherd Dog?
faqs.a: The three largest annual expenses are food ($800–1,200), veterinary care ($400–$1,200 budgeted annually), and pet insurance ($800–1,800 per year). Grooming costs are lower for short-coated breeds managed at home.

faqs.q: How much does a Romanian Mioritic Shepherd Dog cost in the first year?
faqs.a: Year one costs for a Romanian Mioritic Shepherd Dog are significantly higher than subsequent years, typically $2,500–$5,000. This covers the purchase price or adoption fee, initial vet checks, vaccinations, spay/neuter, microchipping, crate, bedding, collar, leads and puppy training classes.

faqs.q: How often should I groom a Romanian Mioritic Shepherd Dog?
faqs.a: Romanian Mioritic Shepherd Dogs need brushing once or twice per week.  Nails should be trimmed every 3–4 weeks. Ears should be checked and cleaned monthly.

faqs.q: Do Romanian Mioritic Shepherd Dogs shed a lot?
faqs.a: Romanian Mioritic Shepherd Dogs shed minimally. A weekly brush is usually sufficient.

faqs.q: What grooming tools does a Romanian Mioritic Shepherd Dog need?
faqs.a: A rubber grooming glove or soft-bristle brush is sufficient for weekly maintenance on the Romanian Mioritic Shepherd Dog's medium coat. Add a nail grinder and ear cleaner for a complete grooming kit.

faqs.q: How often should I bathe a Romanian Mioritic Shepherd Dog?
faqs.a: Every 4–6 weeks is appropriate for most Romanian Mioritic Shepherd Dogs that live indoors. More frequent bathing is needed if they swim or spend time in mud. Over-bathing strips natural skin oils — use a pH-balanced dog shampoo rather than human products.

faqs.q: Are Romanian Mioritic Shepherd Dogs easy to train?
faqs.a: Romanian Mioritic Shepherd Dogs are independent thinkers and can be challenging to train. They respond best to high-value rewards and clear, consistent criteria. A structured puppy class from week one is strongly recommended.

faqs.q: What training method works best for a Romanian Mioritic Shepherd Dog?
faqs.a: Reward-based training using treats, praise and toy rewards is the most effective and well-researched approach for Romanian Mioritic Shepherd Dogs. Clicker training with precise timing works well to mark the exact moment of correct behaviour. Avoid aversive methods — they increase anxiety and often create secondary behavioural problems.

faqs.q: At what age should I start training my Romanian Mioritic Shepherd Dog?
faqs.a: Start training from the day your puppy arrives home, typically at 8 weeks. The 8–16 week window is the most sensitive socialisation period. Enrol in a puppy class within the first two weeks for structured socialisation alongside basic obedience foundations.

faqs.q: How long does it take to train a Romanian Mioritic Shepherd Dog?
faqs.a: Romanian Mioritic Shepherd Dogs can take longer to reach reliable obedience than easier-to-train breeds — expect 3–6 months of consistent daily training for solid basics. Their independent nature means results compound slowly but durably with patience.

faqs.q: What health problems do Romanian Mioritic Shepherd Dogs commonly have?
faqs.a: Romanian Mioritic Shepherd Dogs are most commonly associated with routine age-related conditions. Regular vet checks, appropriate weight management, and breed-specific screening tests help detect issues early. Ask any breeder for health test results before purchasing.

faqs.q: How long do Romanian Mioritic Shepherd Dogs live?
faqs.a: Romanian Mioritic Shepherd Dogs have an average lifespan of 12–14 years. Larger breeds typically have shorter lifespans than smaller breeds. Maintaining a healthy weight and regular vet care are the most impactful factors for longevity.

faqs.q: Are Romanian Mioritic Shepherd Dogs prone to hip dysplasia?
faqs.a: Romanian Mioritic Shepherd Dogs have a moderate-to-elevated risk of hip dysplasia, particularly for large or active breeds. Ask for OFA or PennHIP hip evaluation certificates when buying from a breeder. Weight control and avoiding high-impact exercise during bone growth (under 18 months) reduces risk.

faqs.q: What health tests should a Romanian Mioritic Shepherd Dog puppy have?
faqs.a: At minimum, your Romanian Mioritic Shepherd Dog puppy should have a vet health check, first vaccinations, deworming, and microchipping before coming home. Ask the breeder for parent health certificates relevant to Romanian Mioritic Shepherd Dog-specific conditions. A vet check within 72 hours of bringing your puppy home is recommended to establish a baseline.

faqs.q: Are Romanian Mioritic Shepherd Dogs good with kids?
faqs.a: Romanian Mioritic Shepherd Dogs can be protective and may be cautious around unfamiliar children. Early socialisation with children from puppyhood significantly improves tolerance. Always supervise interactions between dogs and young children.

faqs.q: Do Romanian Mioritic Shepherd Dogs get along with other dogs?
faqs.a: Romanian Mioritic Shepherd Dogs can be selective with other dogs due to their protective nature. Early socialisation in puppy classes and controlled on-lead introductions with other dogs help build positive associations.

faqs.q: Do Romanian Mioritic Shepherd Dogs bark a lot?
faqs.a: Romanian Mioritic Shepherd Dogs tend to be vocal — they may bark at strangers, sounds, or when under-stimulated. Adequate daily exercise and mental enrichment (training sessions, puzzle feeders) significantly reduce nuisance barking. Teaching a "quiet" cue early is worthwhile.

faqs.q: Are Romanian Mioritic Shepherd Dogs good apartment dogs?
faqs.a: Romanian Mioritic Shepherd Dogs can live in apartments if their exercise needs are met consistently. The key variable is owner commitment to daily walks and enrichment — breed size alone doesn't determine apartment suitability.

faqs.q: How much exercise does a Romanian Mioritic Shepherd Dog need per day?
faqs.a: Romanian Mioritic Shepherd Dogs need approximately 45–60 minutes of exercise daily. A structured morning walk and an evening sniff walk usually cover their needs. Mental exercise (training sessions, puzzle feeders) counts toward overall stimulation needs and can reduce restless behaviour.

faqs.q: Are Romanian Mioritic Shepherd Dogs good running partners?
faqs.a: Romanian Mioritic Shepherd Dogs can join you for moderate runs once fully grown. They're better suited to steady 3–5 mile runs than extended distance. Watch for signs of fatigue and always run in cooler hours during summer.

faqs.q: What happens if a Romanian Mioritic Shepherd Dog doesn't get enough exercise?
faqs.a: Romanian Mioritic Shepherd Dogs are less demanding than high-energy breeds, but chronic under-exercise still leads to weight gain and low-level restlessness. Even lower-energy breeds benefit from a consistent daily walk for both physical health and mental stimulation.

faqs.q: Can a Romanian Mioritic Shepherd Dog be off-lead?
faqs.a: Off-lead freedom for a Romanian Mioritic Shepherd Dog depends on recall reliability, not breed alone. Train recall from puppyhood using long-line sessions before progressing to full off-lead. A long-line is recommended as an intermediate step for several months.

faqs.q: How much should I feed my Romanian Mioritic Shepherd Dog?
faqs.a: A Romanian Mioritic Shepherd Dog needs approximately 3–5 cups of dry food per day for an adult, split across two meals. Always follow the feeding guide on your specific formula — calorie density varies significantly between brands. Adjust portions based on body condition: you should be able to feel (but not easily see) the ribs.

faqs.q: How many times a day should I feed a Romanian Mioritic Shepherd Dog?
faqs.a: Adult Romanian Mioritic Shepherd Dogs should eat twice daily. Puppies (under 6 months) need 3–4 smaller meals per day to support growth and prevent hypoglycaemia, particularly in small breeds. For large and giant breeds, twice daily feeding also reduces the risk of bloat (GDV) compared to one large daily meal.

faqs.q: What is the best food for a Romanian Mioritic Shepherd Dog?
faqs.a: Look for a formula carrying an AAFCO adequacy statement for the correct life stage. A named protein source (chicken, turkey, beef, salmon) should appear first in the ingredient list. Medium-energy Romanian Mioritic Shepherd Dogs do well on standard adult maintenance formulas with named protein as the first ingredient.

faqs.q: When should I switch my Romanian Mioritic Shepherd Dog from puppy to adult food?
faqs.a: Large breeds should stay on a large-breed puppy formula until 18–24 months, then transition to an adult formula. Switching too early can disrupt joint development during the growth phase.

faqs.q: Is a Romanian Mioritic Shepherd Dog a good dog for first-time owners?
faqs.a: Romanian Mioritic Shepherd Dogs can be challenging for first-time owners due to their independent temperament. Prior dog experience or professional training classes from the start significantly improves outcomes. Research the breed thoroughly before committing.

faqs.q: Are Romanian Mioritic Shepherd Dogs good family dogs?
faqs.a: Romanian Mioritic Shepherd Dogs can be good family dogs when properly socialised. Their suitability depends more on individual temperament and upbringing than breed alone.

faqs.q: Do Romanian Mioritic Shepherd Dogs do well when left alone?
faqs.a: Romanian Mioritic Shepherd Dogs are more independent than many breeds and generally tolerate alone time better than highly social dogs. Still, aim for no more than 4–6 hours alone for an adult dog, and less for puppies.

faqs.q: How much time do you need for a Romanian Mioritic Shepherd Dog?
faqs.a: Plan for 1.5–2 hours per day dedicated to your Romanian Mioritic Shepherd Dog — covering exercise, training, feeding and general interaction.  The commitment is consistent year-round, not just when convenient.
